_comment: Regulatory profile for Nigeria: the data-protection authority, the grounds on which an impact assessment is required before processing, the retention rule where no statutory period is set, and the breach-notification clock. Read by the compliance generators; the core evaluates the conditions and cites nothing itself. Verify every citation against the current text of the Act and the Directive before filing anything.
law: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025
controllerOfMajorImportance: a controller processing the data of more than two hundred data subjects in six months is of major importance; ministries, departments and agencies are expressly placed at the extra-high tier, and more than five thousand data subjects in six months at the ultra-high tier

dpiaTriggers.ground: GAID 2025 Art. 28(3)(l): a legal instrument or policy requiring the processing of personal data of members of the general public
dpiaTriggers.because: a residents' registration law is such an instrument; this trigger applies to every deployment

dpiaTriggers.ground: GAID 2025 Art. 28(3): sensitive or highly personal data, including biometrics
GAID 2025 Art. 28(3) and Schedule 6: vulnerable data subjects
dpiaTriggers.because: a register of residents reaches children, the displaced and people without digital access

dpiaTriggers.ground: NDPA 2023 s.37: decisions by automated means producing legal or similarly significant effects
dpiaTriggers.because: the accepted binding and residence methods permit an issuance decision with no person in the loop

dpiaTriggers.ground: GAID 2025 Art. 28(3): new technology for processing
dpiaTriggers.because: verifiable credentials, offline verification and federated sign-in are new to most state registers

retentionLapseWhereUnset: where the law sets no period, GAID 2025 Art. 49(3) lapses storage six months after purpose (subject to the exception in 49(4)); set residency.retention.residencyDays or document the statutory period relied on
thirdPartySharing: GAID 2025 Art. 41(9): sharing with a third party requires explicit, revocable consent stating purpose, scope and duration
breachSubjectNotification: affected data subjects are notified immediately where the risk to them is high
hostingNote: the national cloud computing guideline approved in 2026 makes in-country hosting the default for government data at its higher classifications and encourages states to adopt it
